As per the Draft Forum Policies found here: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies

Site members who can greenlight concepts are those who fulfill one or more of the following criteria:

  • They are on the Butterfly Squad Roster list of reviewers.
  • They have an entry in the Authors' Pages list or they qualify for an Author Page (they have written 3 or more successful mainsite pages).
  • They have been featured in the Reviewers' Spotlight.
  • They are a staff member.

You may want to consider messaging users listed from above to see if they'd be interested in looking at your concept. Also, reviewers would usually make it obvious when they greenlight something (such as stating that they are giving the concept a greenlight).

item.title: Echos eines Hoffest
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History

Page Layout (Optional): Video logs, interviews, document references and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: The city of Mainz (Germany) gathers annually during the Pentecost day for a party in which the citizens anomalously change their behaviour as if they were in the 12th century for a day. After an incident, the Foundation intervenes only to provoke this change to become permanent.

Central Narrative: During the Pentecost day in Mainz, its citizens celebrate the festivity in a nearby location, where upon access they show an altered behaviour proper of the European nobility in the 12th century, such as a firm code of honour; and participate in joust tournaments. By the following day, citizens involved have no related memories.

+ Show
- Hide

This activity went under the radar of the Foundation until a Turkish attendant was found dead after one of these events with the words "Deus Vult" engraved on his chest. The following year, Foundation found out about these effects with on-site live-recordings. Identifying a potential assault similar to the previous year, a task force bursts into the gathering, disbanding all attendants. This time affected individuals keep their memories and the behaviour displayed during this event. Chaos ensues due to the cultural clash with modern Germany.

The next Pentecost day, affected population gathers again, live-recordings showing that the activities performed are exactly the same as in the previous year. Once the celebration finishes, all attendants return to the normal behaviour. Foundation decides not to interrupt this event, but stops population from attending by fencing the site. Instead, attendants move to nearby Ingelheim, where anomalous natural catastrophes result in hundreds of casualties. The Foundation allows the event to occur at the usual location, however impeding the attendance to vulnerable individuals.

Recording logs interview seemingly a monk, who seems to be responsible of these events. Back in 1184, Kaiser Barbarossa hosted a huge fest in that same location. By law, Konrad was to be seated by the Kaiser during the ceremonies, however he was substituted in a political move by the Archbishop of Cologne. Resentful, he condemned the dishonour, ensuring that that day would be repeated over and over until the Kaiser rectified his mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is a story about timely cultural clash, by bringing a huge population from the past to the current days. It is also a story about resentment and, literally, holding a grudge.

Additional Notes: Based on the 1184 Mainzer Hoftag. Kaiser Barbarossa might be SCP-125-DE.

item.title: Re: The Dover Demon
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

So my concern here is that you're trying to put too many historical events together without something that connects them directly. At this moment, this seems like a historical lesson with a 'funny' character to explain it, like a documentary for kids or something. I would suggest to pick only one event and focus on it. Maybe the demon had something to do with it? Maybe its obsession with shoes comes from something that happen in that event?

Also, I feel like the anomaly isn't interesting on its own. Like, the only backstory it hs is regarding human history, and all of its abilities feel like they're just there so it can travel through history without being noticed. Again, this feels like a documentary for kids. Also, I agree with JamaisJ's point about the Foundation having better sources.

Overall, I think you should choose just one historical event and then make your anomaly to interact with it.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Re: Arctic Horror SCP
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

personnel are to be deterred from ingesting

Why? What happens when you eat it? Sure, it has healing properties, but why should they stop the personnel from eating it at all costs? How long do these properties last? You should explain them more in-depth.

one instance is recovered by a researcher and a containment engineer.

Why did they send a researcher and an engineer? Wouldn't it be best to send and MTF? I suggest to change this to either two MTF members or that the researcher and the engineer got trapped during the storm and they're waiting for rescue.

but the researcher had consumed the herb prior to death

Why did he do so? Didn't the herb help him to recover? Why did he wish to be cremated if he had already consumed the herb? I really feel like this part is just here to eventually get to the dissection scene. And I feel like the dissection scene is just there to shock the reader without too much effort.

I would suggest to change the anomaly's properties so they have something to do with 'survival'. That way you could add some arguments between the two regarding if they should use the anomaly or not. Also, some personal drama would help a lot in this concept.

Overall, I like this concept, but I think you should focus on the struggle to survive rather than trying to shock the reader.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look!

item.title: SCP Greenlight - The Marvelous Transformation Alchemy Machine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Comedy

Page Layout: Standard, with several reports included from uses of the SCP.

Elevator Pitch: A coin-slot 'entertainment' machine that allows the user to create transformation-inducing fluids using alchemy.

Central Narrative: The device is initially used to create relatively 'tame' creations (improved mental acuity, stamina, etc.), similar to SCP-294, before more biologically traumatic and transformational contents are created, with a particularly clever researcher versed in alchemy theory creating a fluid that results in [REDACTED].

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A device that uses historic alchemy in order to create transformative concoctions, requiring only a US 25 cent quarter, and a nontrivial amount of mercury.

Additional Notes: Some aspects I'm concerned are the potential "wunderkind" status of such a device to create fluids that provide benefits to the user without much difficulty. I also am unsure how to make device 'dangerous' outside accidental or deliberate misuse.

item.title: Re: The Emotional Reality Bender
item.content:encoded:
+ open for crit
- Close

This SCP was born as an reality bender also known as a type green. Unlike most type greens she is rather limited with her ability's seemingly only being able to affect a few things at an time depending on her mood. When she is sad she can't affect anything and when she's angry or scared she can affect many things. Although how she can affect these objects is not limited.

Emotion-based skips have been done countless times already, the only difference is this one's a reality bender who completely depends on emotions for her to be able to bend reality. I'd assume this type green is completely unstable and unpredictable due to their conditions and I'd like to see what you could do with the idea. What's the relationship between her and her abilities? Can she control her abilities? How would her abilities amplify and behave based on her emotions at the moment (ex. If she's confused would reality and hume levels around her be off the charts? If she's angry would she go in a rage and be able to utilize her abilities, but not exactly control what would happen because of her not having a focused line of thougt? Is there a dominant emotion? Is she essentially a jack of all trades, but being limited by her emotions one at a time? Etc, etc.)?

Within the article it will talk about a policy on how staff should treat the SCP such as how they should talk down to her and to try to keep her in a sad mood pretty much. This and a combination of test some being somewhat cruel (Researchers doing test without permission) will make her unstable emotionally which may lead to her becoming more dangerous.

A policy? Do you mean a containment procedure or general protocol for dealing with her? "Researchers doing a test without permission"? What tests would researchers need to do that they wouldn't just normally do? If you wanna write a cruel Foundation by all means go for it, but this really just doesn't make sense. What kind of "tests without permission" are we talking about here? Besides that is there anything else you plan on doing with the story? Is there gonna be any development for the type-green so we actually care about her when she's being cruelly treated and not just being a 2-dimensional bad guy.

I'm hoping to hook the reader with a series of interviews and tests within the article. I also hope that the reader gets invested with the SCP it's self and to perhaps even feel bad for her or to think that the things done to keep her sad is for the best.

Shouldn't this go in the page layout section? Anyways, you gotta tell us how you're gonna develop the type-green and make us feel bad for her. What's her background? Does she even want this? Etc.

Overall: The idea of an anomalous entity based entirely around emotions has been done so many times before so you're essentially forced into making a compelling narrative but it feels like it's not there. I can tell you clearly have an idea of what you wanna do and that you want to explore these deeper themes like ethics, authoritarianism, and emotions. You have to tell people how you're gonna do it though. I'll just repeat myself with the same advice I gave above but I hope you took my suggestions and criticism into consideration, gl with the idea, just shoot me a wikidot pm or find me in one of the IRC channels if you want me to give a follow-up review.

- Close

Forum thread: The Emotional Reality Bender

item.title: Re: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.content:encoded:
First and foremost, this is my opinion as one writer to another. Although I am a member of SCPWiki staff I am not speaking to you in any way shape or form as a member of staff. This is just two people talking writing.

As respectfully as possible, this is a tremendous amount of labor and thought-process to undertake for something you have barely begun drafting. The types of minutia you're looking to hammer out could disappear like a puff of smoke in the wind if you fall at writing the underlying SCP.

While I am not a member of the licensing team and do not have any formal opinions or recommendations regarding licensing, I do have several years experiencing on the site including providing feedback and writing successful articles.

You're going to look and feel very silly if you go to all this trouble for something that is summarily deleted. Do not put the cart before the horse with dreams of a smash hit SCP and your own cult Twitch following that blooms from it.

Dreaming big and having ambitions are wonderful, and I hope you have a chance to stare down your goals in life and go for it one day. But dreams are also built upon the little steps along the way. You have no twitch channel if you have no article. Write it first. Make it good. Make it great. Then maybe we can talk about this.

If you cannot see one existing without the other, then that's all the more reason to step back and reconsider what you're doing.

item.title: [Need Greenlighting] [First SCP Article] "Step 2"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a small bottle of vegetable oil that, when applied to user's skin, causes them to float. Users will continue to float until they either hit a ceiling or the oil gets washed off. Upon hitting a ceiling or a limit, the user oil will continue to rise until it is off the user, where it'll then fall. The user will too fall due to the oil being removed.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX causes user's to controllably levitate upwards, people who consume SCP-XXXX will continually float upwards until they hit a ceiling. If the user continues to float upwards, they will eventually extricate it outwards, causing the user and the extrication to fall. If people who have consumed SCP-XXXX hit a limiter or a ceiling, they will be pulled up forcefully until their organs containing the oil rupture out of the consumer. causing the user to fall.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is seemingly safe, but due to the container continuing to fill it's environment, it could cause the end of our known universe.

Additional Notes: It's a pretty basic SAFE article.

item.title: Re: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

While I really like the idea of a creepy house with creepy kids inside a creepy forest, I have a few concerns. First, the idea of dragon-like creatures seems off with the rest of the article. Like, you have all this creepy atmosphere, this mysterious house, and then… DRAGONS! I think you should try to make the reader to feel horror without showing the "true" monster. Maybe you could say that they're shapeshifting creatures that can't shapeshift while on our realm? Maybe they don't have a 'true' form?

Now, the motives of the children are a little fuzzy. Why do they want to kidnap people? What's in the other side of the door? Is its an interdimesional portal? Some kind of "gate to Hell"? Also, why are they trapped inside of the house? Why does the house teleports if they're supposed to be trapped? You should explain those things in your idea post.

Furthermore, you may want to read this essay about horror in the SCP format. It's very interesting if you wanna write a horror article.

Overall, I like the feeling of creepy horror you have here, you some things feel a little off.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look!

item.title: Re: Let's Go on an Adventure! (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

My primary concern is that this idea seems to have various clichés of "people going into a journey". I don't see any type of interesting thing regarding this 'adventure', and that's mainly because you don't say almost anything regarding the chimera. From my point of view, it seems to appear out of nothing just to be some kind of antagonist for the adventure. I think you should explain the chimera's backstory, if there's one. What are its motives? Is it just evil just because 'why not'?

Now, the 'underground city' also seems to appear out of the blue. Like, why do all of these explorers needed to form a city? couldn't they just go to their homes to live in glory for the rest of their lives?

My last concern is that I don't see how are you going to portray all of this. Are you planning to write journals, exploration logs…? Like, how do they know the backpack is going to lose its properties one day? Is there a prophecy or something? Also, what are you going to focus on? Are you planning to follow the adventure of someone in particular? Are you planning to show various attempts at killing the chimera?

My advice here is that you should cut the city out and focus on the chimera. Maybe you could write that it's a legendary beast or something. You should expand on the motives of the beast for killing all of those explorers. Of course, it's all up to you, but I would suggest to remove either the city or the chimera.

Overall, this feels like another "fantasy adventure" with the Foundation logo on it. I think you need to specify what you're going to focus on.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

This just feels like the classic "thing that does a thing", and what should make up for the generally dry concept in comedic tone and/or narrative that you wanna go for seems missing, if anything it'd be disturbing considering how the box makes people want to open, record an unboxing video for the whole internet to see, then immediately gets brutally murdered.

I do like that tacked on gumball bit, I can see myself chuckling if done comedically. Like making fun of the incredibly exaggerated and annoying reactions that are present in almost every one of those types of videos nowadays by portraying it with the unboxers reacting to the effects of the gumball, giving a reaction and being all hyped up to then immediately being killed off.

The anart part of the concept does intrigue me and some compelling commentary could be made with the article from the anartist's point of view but also subtly made by you as well. I don't see how this is enough for a central narrative though, tell us about what you wanna do with the anart element besides just being an anart anomaly. What about the people affected by the anomaly itself, have there been any survivors and if so have they gone through some sort of trauma? How do you plan on portraying the comedic elements?

Overall, you got some compelling ideas but besides that the main concept is lacking in being interesting or unique, like I said it's essentially just another "thing that does a thing". You don't tell us how you're gonna implement the comedy bit or give us anything that could make up for the flat idea. Only advice I have on how you could make it more appealing I've already stated, what's would the point of view of affected individuals be, mixing commentary on the unboxing scene with comedy, and exploring the anart piece of the concept and maybe the anartist's too, like a motivation.

Well that's all I got, I hope you cleanup the idea with some of the suggestions I made and manage to move foward with it to the mainlist. Have a good one.

item.title: Re: SCP-5144 Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Hello there! I'll swing by and give you my thoughts.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

The Time Lord

A Dr. Who fan, I see.

So the basic concept is that it's just some person who can control time in some undescribed way. That's too vague and underdeveloped and doesn't offer anything.

The longing to live free and in peace driving a man to extremes.

That's not a plot. That's a theme. That's something a plot's supposed to be going for, not actually a plot.

Subject has repeatedly gone back in time, killed the SCP Foundation's Founders, but the Foundation keeps forming anyway with a different SCP-001 causing the founding.

I don't see how doing this would bring freedom and peace, considering the Foundation also contains dangerous, reality and world ending anomalies. Containing them to make sure peace is kept.

It's actually a good thing the Foundation keeps coming back somehow despite his efforts.

Yeah, I'm not really feeling this. This reads like a vague pitch for a young adult book but without having anything expanded upon, not like an SCP.

On a tangential note, I should mention that humanoids are incredibly difficult to do and I don't recommend it as a first SCP. It's possible for a first SCP, in case you insist on pursuing this. Just difficult.

Anywho, I apologise if this was a tad harsh. I hope I helped and I bid you a good day! 👍

item.title: Storm of crows
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous phenomenon in Basney, Connecticut (a fictional town), where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.

More
Not more

The highest record of crows at one point in the town was 84,784 crows (for reference, the town has a population of 1,812).
When a house in the town is damaged, it will start to heal by regeneration, although minor damages take less time to heal than major damages. Damages won't be healed as an identical version of the house, leaving flaws, such as furniture that was never there, irregular wallpaper patterns, doors or stairs leading to nothing, rooms or objects with irregular shape/or proportions, etc.

A unique crow will be "assigned" to a specific house in the town for every house. These crows are distinguishable by their single white feather. These crows (nicknamed "Protector Crows") will interact with the occupants of the homes they are assigned to, showing more compassion and intelligence than an average crow.

These crows are also the first sign that the anomalous phenomenon that is SCP-XXXX (the massive crow migration) is about to happen.

However, the foundation discovered that when a crow is killed, the house's self-repairing is assigned to stops entirely.

The foundation only knows what they get from observing the crows and testing, not really caring about anything other than keeping secrecy. So the story comes.

Central Narrative: The narrative is presented in a personal journal belonging to a young teenage girl named Sahra, who has lived in the town her whole life but will be in the first instance of SCP_XXXX. She lives with her parents and little sister, Rosa, and little brother, Eric.

more
not more

Keep in mind I'm going over the most important parts.

Their protector, crow, come to their house. Rosa names them Chip because they brought a corn chip as a gift to their windowsill.

The next day when Sahra goes to school, she notes that there are usually some crows in this town, but not this much. The crow population now is around 142.

Soon a large and irregular migration of crows to the town is detected by the local news. The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. But none of their methods are working as every time one crow leaves, more come in replacement.

Sarah's dad one day breaks a door hinge while slamming a door shut. He later calls one of his friends to help fix it when he gets back home, but it's fixed when they get back home.

Soon the crows outnumber the town's population 12 to 1. Sarah mistakes a large number of crows on a tree as leaves, as a way to show how many of them there are.

The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. They use fireworks, predators, big hunting, but none of them work as every time one goes away, more come to replace it. Soon the crow's number in the thousands.

One day a car crashes into Sarah's house and injures chip. They find chip dead, and the part the car hit started rapidly attempting to fix itself. The broken part starts to start to expand in size and uses the wrong building materials (like concrete for a door, plastic for the grade door, and even flesh). the crow's brain essentially went on overdrive mode right before dying, irregularly snd rapidly fixing any damaged parts. This is when the foundation is informed of something majorly anomalous happening.

The foundation came to the town, amnesticize everybody, move them out, create a cover story as to why there were so many crows, and find Sarah's journal.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An article with a light story isn't as common as Lovecraftian horror and Apollyon class SCPs. And if you're looking for some big answer about why the crows go there or a dark secret about the town, you're missing the point.

Additional Notes: Sarah and her family were in the first instance of SCP-XXXX which is why the foundation hadn't known about the anomaly. I am still hoping to expand on the idea so any criticism will help.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your critique.

The plot holes you described are ones that I tried to iron out but had a hard time fixing within the 400 word limit. The best way for me to fix your plot holes is to explain them outside of the actual thread. With this, I would like to list the fixes to your listed issues within this response.

Also, this is a big fold out.

+ Plot Hole Breakdown
- Explanations

The anomaly is located within Bryce Canyon National Park, where a dimension (at a certain time of night) anomalously takes the place of the park.

The entire park is not affected by the anomaly, the park is more of an established perimeter. The Amphitheater region of the park is the one anomalously affected, and even then it doesn’t inhabit the entire region. See the region itself doesn’t change, it’s more of the foyer to the dimension. At a certain point deep in the region, a person will pass this foyer and enter the dimension. There’s no defined door or riff through space, it is not visible from above or from a vantage point, at some point within the Amphitheater the person will enter a dimension without knowing. Of course this explanation would obviously be hard to fit within the 400 word limit, which is why I explained it as such.

and individuals who have died and do not profess to any religion or cult.

Understandably it comes out of nowhere for the Foundation to know this criteria without research. I meant to describe how the Foundation did some investigating to find that some of these people were deceased and found inside the dimension. All in all with this quote, I want to say that the Foundation did their research while exploring the dimension and concluded that the individuals inside of it were atheists and non-cult followers that are identified as deceased. Believe me when I say that I wanted to describe this, but again, limits.

After a D-Class was able to return with her daughter however, research is strangely ramped up by Harry, as he becomes more and more unprofessional.

As you mentioned, there is some confusion of whether or not this was intentional or accidental. I would like to say that Harry requested for the D-Class to bring someone from the dimension back to the real world, with the results surprising Harry. Now in terms of how this happens, it’s mostly on how this dimension works.

Essentially, every person has a predetermined death date, kind of like a Book of Life scenario. However, some people die too early, meaning they did not correctly follow their life story. This is the case for the D-Class’ daughter, who was not suppose to die at a young age and thus is able to be brought back from the dimension. This is also the case for Harry’s wife, who was meant to die in a containment breach and thus cannot be brought back from the dead.

This was meant to be flushed out in the draft, and I had no idea how to condense all this information for this plot hole to be flushed out.

The MTF is picked off as the soldiers are taken to different caverns by the demons.

This plot hole can be flushed out with how these demons operate. These demons are actually non-aggressive in nature and are stationary when not provoked. See when a person enters the dimension or is manifested within it, the demons will begin to stare at them. Most of the time these demons will do nothing, but other times a demon will suddenly be aggressive and will bring the person to a cavern. That demon essentially judged the person and found them guilty, with their punishment being whatever cavern they are taken to.

With this context, I would like to say that the MTF is not dead upon entering, but they are officially dead when taken to a cavern. Following the “death date” explanation, the MTF was meant to die in the dimension and immediately taken to their respective cavern.

but Harry is the last one remaining in the group.

Following the previous explanation, Harry was not meant to die in the dimension like the MTF. Harry’s sort of “life story” was suppose to end in his suicide, not by a demon killing him. This quote didn’t have an elaborate explanation that had to be left out, I just thought this would be self-explanatory. Of course with your critique on it, I can see why this quote needs some explanation.


All in all, the plot holes you flushed out were ones I knew existed but had no idea how to explain within the 400 word limit. I hope this post will allow you to understand why I didn’t make any changes to the article and why I opted to make a post to explain each issue. Hope this is suffice.

item.title: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.content:encoded:
This SCP is a reality-affecting entity that was captured by an English Earl (or baron, I'm unsure) at some point in the 1800s, probably around 1850 or later. I think the upper limit should probably be 1900 when the British nobility was dying off.

The earl in question had an interest in Psychology, and when he captured the anomalous entity he realised it's potential to help cure his patients. He slowly reformed the entity over time to genuinely come to enjoy helping humans, and it continued when he died.

A problem is is that the SCP mostly focuses on Therapeutic techniques, which from what i can gather came about more when Freud entered onto the scene, which i think was 1880 or so, which is a little early i think. It is also set in Britain, so it would be whatever theories were popular there.

So I'm currently unsure what theories of treatment this entity may subscribe to, as it would depend on which theories were around when it was being trained under this earl.
